narrative: Markets are in a risk-off regime following the sudden resignation and ousting of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid DOJ espionage and smuggling probes. This leadership crisis has triggered a sharp sell-off in AI-related equities and heightened regulatory uncertainty. Simultaneously, investors are grappling with hawkish signals from the Fed, as sticky inflation and a resilient labor market push terminal rate expectations above 5%. Geopolitical tensions, particularly regarding US-China chip export controls and regional instability, are further weighing on sentiment. Consequently, capital is rotating out of high-growth tech while crude oil rallies on supply and geopolitical concerns.

Nasdaq.why: The index is under significant pressure due to the Nvidia leadership crisis and broader uncertainty surrounding AI sector concentration and regulatory risks.

S&P 500.why: The index is declining as investors digest the AI sector volatility and the broader market impact of the Nvidia leadership transition.

Gold.why: Spot gold has declined approximately 2.7% to $3,882 per ounce.

Oil.why: Crude oil is rallying, with WTI up 2.8% and Brent up 3.5%, driven by geopolitical developments and supply concerns.

priced_in: Increased volatility for the semiconductor and AI sectors
A 25bps rate hike for December with growing caution regarding a 50bps move
Heightened regulatory and legislative risk for technology companies
Increased risk for AI-related credit and potential future defaults
debates: Whether the AI infrastructure build-out remains robust despite the leadership crisis at Nvidia
The sustainability of capital expenditure in the AI sector given rising costs of capital
watch_next: Core PCE and PPI data releases
Jensen Huang's scheduled testimony before Congress
